name: Kentucky

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 6 months after appointment of the personal representative, or within 2 years after death if no personal representative is appointed (KRS 396.011(1), effective June 29, 2021).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative may distribute the estate 6 months after qualification (KRS 395.190); an informal final settlement may be filed any time after 6 months from appointment (KRS 395.605(3)).

smallEstate.text: No affidavit procedure: the District Court may dispense with administration and transfer the assets when the surviving spouse's (or children's) $30,000 exemption under KRS 391.030, alone or with preferred claims paid by them, equals or exceeds the distributable assets (KRS 395.455, as amended effective July 15, 2026; KRS 391.030(1)(c)).

simplified.text: Order dispensing with administration (KRS 395.455); informal final settlement without hearing when the fiduciary is sole beneficiary or all beneficiaries sign verified waivers, after 6 months (KRS 395.605).

filingFee.text: Probate court costs are fixed by statute and Supreme Court rule; the amount was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Compensation of an executor or administrator may not exceed 5% of the value of the decedent's personal estate plus 5% of the income collected; the court may allow fair and reasonable extra compensation for extraordinary services, real estate or death-tax work on non-probate property (KRS 395.150).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney fee schedule; the attorney's fee must be disclosed in settlements (KRS 395.605(1)(e)) and is allowed by the court as reasonable.

uncertain: Kentucky has no general small-estate affidavit; smallEstate.limit = 30000 is the spouse/children exemption that triggers dispensing with administration (KRS 391.030, 395.455), not a general cap.
Kentucky probate filing fee not read; filingFee.amount = null.
